desc: Derive and prove the structural lemmas: condition for disjointness (R_i < L_j or R_j < L_i), connected component characterization, and bound on shortest-path length (in hops) within a component.
Formulate the minimum-weight path as a case analysis (direct edge; s→x→t; s→x→y→t) and identify exactly which candidate sets must be minimized over.
Design the precomputation: sorting by L and R, prefix/suffix minimum weight structures, so each candidate set's minimum weight vertex can be queried in O(log N).
Handle edge cases: excluding endpoints from intermediate candidates, components where s,t are in different components (answer -1), and verifying the hop bound covers all cases.
Implement the full solution in Python with fast I/O, following the derived formulas, targeting O((N+Q) log N).
Validate: run provided samples, and stress-test against a brute-force BFS/Dijkstra solution on small random inputs (many seeds), fixing any discrepancies.

Fix the component computation in the code: replace the incorrect sweep-based component logic with the universal-vertex criterion (vertex i is isolated iff L_i ≤ min R over all j≠i AND R_i ≥ max L over all j≠i; all non-universal vertices form one component, each universal vertex is its own component), keeping the validated per-query logic unchanged, and produce the final corrected code.
